messages:
incident-bot: PAGER ALERT: elevated 5xx error rate observed for inference-prod (us-west-2). Root symptom: model-runner processes crashing / OOMs causing gateway 502/504 spikes. Pager: @sam-oncall. Runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/runtime-5xx. Please ack and triage.
sam-oncall: acked. I'm on it. tagging @jordan-sre and @maya-runtime. Any ongoing customer impact metrics yet?
jordan-sre: seeing gateway 502 rate up ~18% over baseline for last 6m, timeouts up too. Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: gptx-open-13b). No deploys in last hour per deploy-bot.
maya-runtime: attaching recent logs from the model-runner on node-rt-3:
```
[2025-03-12T14:03:21Z] model-runner[pid=8123] ERROR: segfault at 0x0
[2025-03-12T14:03:21Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 8123 (model-runner) total-vm: 124G, anon-rss: 98G
[2025-03-12T14:03:22Z] gateway: upstream 502 from 10.4.9.3: inference runtime crashed
```
maya-runtime: same pattern on 3 nodes, memory climbs before crash, looks like KV cache growth + long seq requests.
max-eng: can we trigger fallback routing to smaller quantized variant? Console has a canary fallback for gptx-open-13b -> gptx-13b-quant-fast. If we route traffic, we reduce memory pressure quickly.
jordan-sre: agree. Also lowering per-request batch cap and disabling long-seq batching temporarily.
sam-oncall: @ops-bot can you start rerouting 40% traffic to fallback and scale up dedicated pools 2x? also reduce batch_size global to 8.
ops-bot: Scaling action started: increased dedicated pool for inference-prod by +2 nodes. Reroute: updating routing policy to send 40% to gptx-13b-quant-fast at 14:10Z.
ana-cs: customer-impact note — CS dashboard shows ~120 accounts experiencing degraded responses; 5 customers have reported errors via support. I'll open a status message if mitigation takes >30m.
maya-runtime: applied transient config to runtime: kvcache eviction threshold lowered from 80%->60%, enabled aggressive GC for cache; will monitor.
jordan-sre: monitoring shows 5xx dropping to ~6% after reroute & scale at 14:12Z. Latency stabilized for fallback but a few timeouts persist on older connections.
sam-oncall: good. please keep traces and pprof collected for the crashed nodes — we need heap profiles and last-request traces.
maya-runtime: uploading heap profiles to S3: s3://redwood-dumps/incident-3198884444/ — files: node-rt-1.heap.gz, node-rt-2.heap.gz
deploy-bot: No active deploys. Previous deploy (service/ingress) at 2025-03-12T12:50Z.
max-eng: plan: 1) continue reroute until crash rates <1% for 20m 2) run postmortem, prioritize KV cache leak hypothesis 3) consider hotfix to cap per-request cache allocation and reject >16k token requests on this variant.
sam-oncall: accepted. i'll stay on for next 30m then handoff to @jordan-sre if stable. @ana-cs prepare customer comms draft for status page.
ana-cs: drafting now — will include impacted routes, mitigation steps, ETA for full recovery: 1-2 hours.
jordan-sre: timeline update 14:25Z — 5xx at 1.8%, starting to see one-off OOM on remaining legacy nodes. Suggest cordon node-rt-2 and replace with fresh instance.
ops-bot: cordon/replace initiated for node-rt-2. Replacement node healthy and joined pool at 14:31Z.
sam-oncall: leaving handoff notes: mitigations applied (reroute 40%, scale +2, kvcache GC, batch cap 8). artifacts: heap dumps in S3, logs in /var/log/model-runner/incident-3198884444. Next oncall: @jordan-sre. Please escalate to eng if OOMs resume after full recovery window.
jordan-sre: taking over. creating incident doc and postmortem ticket.
ana-cs: posted initial status update to status.redwood.com — will push update if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
maya-runtime: monitoring continuing, set alert for kvcache growth threshold at 50% now.
sam-oncall: resolved? Not closed yet — leave open until stable for 60m. Thanks everyone for quick responses. :heart:
